subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency — recap + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lars Jensen <lars.jensen@nordbank.com>
Cc: NordBank Compliance <compliance@nordbank.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency — recap + next steps

Hi Lars — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay coordinated.

What we heard:
- Primary requirement: All inference processing and customer data must remain in the EU for regulatory/compliance reasons.
- Secondary: interest in predictable throughput for peak batch workloads; potential need for on-prem in high-security vaulting scenarios.
- Evaluation criteria: data residency guarantees, encryption/KMS controls, audit logs, and SLOs for latency.

Redwood options (high level):
1) Hosted API (EU region):
   - Pros: fastest to start, usage-based pricing, EU region (eu-west-1) inference endpoints available.
   - Considerations: control plane metadata (billing/usage aggregation) may traverse our global control plane unless you opt into our Private control plane add-on. We can provide a Data Processing Addendum and technical note on control-plane locality.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
   - Pros: dedicated GPU pools; we can deploy Dedicated capacity in your preferred cloud region (EU) for predictable throughput and isolation.
   - Considerations: longer lead time and minimum commit.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - Pros: Full control — customer-managed VPC or on-prem — control plane can be hosted in your network, customer KMS, and no outbound control-plane data by default. Recommended if you need strict EU-only control-plane and data residency.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short comparison (redwood-hosted-vs-private-summary.pdf), our latest SOC2 Type II (SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026.pdf), and a draft mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-nordbank.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep dive / capacity scoping (Aditya can run through traffic shapes, seq lengths, and latency SLOs) — are you available early next week?
- If legal wants to start redlines on the DPA, I’ll loop in our legal lead (Lauren).

Thanks — happy to adjust based on any missing items.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Lars Jensen <lars.jensen@nordbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 17:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency — recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — that was very helpful. A couple clarifying Qs:
1) For Hosted API in EU, can you confirm that inference requests (input + output) and logs will not leave the EU region under normal operation? We need a firm statement for the compliance review.
2) You mentioned the control plane possibly traversing outside the EU — what metadata specifically would be sent, and is there an option to opt-out or restrict that?
3) For APAC customers we have some subsidiaries — do you have APAC region availability (or partners) for the Hosted path?

Also, can you confirm whether caching/prefix KV is ever stored outside region boundaries for performance reasons?

If you can send short answers and the SOC2 we can share with our compliance team.

— Lars
Lars Jensen
Head of Cloud Platforms, NordBank ASA
lars.jensen@nordbank.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lars Jensen <lars.jensen@nordbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency — recap + next steps

Hi Lars — quick answers inline and next steps. Looping in Aditya (solutions/infra) for the technical deep-dive and Lauren (legal) for DPA/redlines.

1) EU Hosted inference locality:
   - We run inference in our eu-west-1 region endpoints; inference input/output and model state (including KV cache for active requests) remain in-region. For compliance language we can provide an EU data residency attestation that states processing and storage for inference payloads are confined to the EU region for Hosted EU endpoints.

2) Control plane metadata:
   - Examples: aggregate usage metrics, billing counters, and non-sensitive routing telemetry.
   - Options: we offer a Private control plane add-on (part of Private deployment) which keeps the control plane in your VPC/region; alternatively we can sign a DPA and restrict telemetry retention. If you require zero control-plane egress, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the recommended path.

3) APAC availability:
   - We have upcoming APAC regions (planned Q1 2027) and can support APAC via Dedicated or Private deployments sooner via partner cloud. Aditya can explain timing and partner options in the technical call.

Caching: KV/prefix caches used for in-flight inference are created per-region and are not replicated cross-region by default. Cross-region routing is an opt-in fallback for availability (configured by policy) — it’s disabled by default for EU-hosted endpoints.

Attachments/links: SOC2 and the comparison deck are attached again. Lauren — when you get a moment, can you share the DPA and notes about control-plane telemetry?

Next step options:
- Technical deep-dive: Wed 10/28 or Thu 10/29 (Aditya) — proposed 60min to collect sample traffic and discuss Dedicated sizing.
- Legal: We can route a DPA + contract redlines via DocuSign; happy to start earlier if you send initial redlines.

Thanks — we’ll get a MAP in place once we confirm timing.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-private-summary.pdf, SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026.pdf, mutual-action-plan-nordbank.xlsx

- Current traffic profile (QPS, average and p95 seq length, burst windows)
- Latency SLOs and example endpoints (sync vs batch)
- Dedicated sizing and region placement options (EU private subnet vs dedicated in partner cloud)
- KMS integration and key rotation process for Private/Dedicated

Available slots: Thu 10/29 09:00-10:30 PT or Fri 10/30 14:00-15:30 PT. If those don’t work, share a few windows and we’ll accommodate.

Action items for you before the call: sample request rate (requests/min), typical token lengths, and any peak batch/async windows.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
